julia.peopleops: Quick loop-in. Employee on unpaid parental leave waived benefits at OE and is returning 2024-08-01. They want health reinstated effective 8/1 with no coverage gap. What's our standard for LOA-return re-enrolls and retro effective dates? Any limits on backdating and how do we handle missed employee premiums?
samuel.lee: Short answer: submit a QLE for LOA return within 30 days and put in HRIS transaction `LOA_RETURN_REENROLL` with requested effective_date. Carriers differ on retro windows (often up to 60 days max). If carrier permits retro, benefits set the effective date to requested date and payroll can do a catch-up. If carrier denies retro, coverage starts when carrier processes the enrollment.
hris-bot: System note: max system backdate request = 60 days. Required docs: LOA approval memo, signed QLE form, dependent proof if adding. Use benefit codes (MED_BASE, MED_SPOUSE, HSA_EMP).
payroll-bot: Payroll process: we can do one-time catch-up or spread the missed deductions across remaining pay periods. Need these fields before payroll cutoff (T-5 business days): `employee_id`, `benefit_code`, `effective_date`, `employee_premium_amount`, `spread_periods` (optional). Example ticket payload:
``nbenefit_code: MED_SPOUSE
effective_date: 2024-08-01
employee_premium_amount: 98.30
payroll_action: spread_over_4
```
maria.manager: Confirming employee Jordan Patel returns 8/1 and is adding spouse. I have LOA docs and QLE signed; I'll upload now.
julia.peopleops: Great. I'll open HRIS ticket and attach docs + payroll journal snippet. Will ask Jordan if they prefer single catch-up or spread. Will update thread when carrier responds.
